full_judgment: 10. The intention of the legislature, as out-lined in Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, is clear to prevent any outsiders from encroaching upon the ownership and possession of the rightful co-sharers. This ensures that the legitimate co-sharers can continue to enjoy their property without interference from others. The right of pre-emption on the basis of the petitioner being a co-sharer of the tenancy must be proved to the hilt. One cannot succeed on establishing a prima facie case. When the dispute has to be finally adjudicated, the proof of the claim must be established by cogent and reliable evidence.
